positions.subject: q:government/expand-mayoral-authority
positions.summary: His campaign site recommends Yes on Proposition F, which would let the Mayor hire and fire most department heads, saying the Mayor should be able to act as the boss; his GrowSF questionnaire says the Mayor should be able to hire and fire the Police Chief unilaterally.

citations.locator: How I'm Voting, San Francisco's local ballot measures, Prop F

citations.quote: If we’re going to treat the Mayor like the boss, we should let them actually be the boss, including hiring and firing department heads.
citations.locator: How I'm Voting, Prop F: Changes to Executive Branch Management

citations.quote: First, the Mayor should have the ability to hire and fire the Police Chief unilaterally.
citations.locator: Your Policy Goals: Will the power of the office of Supervisor be enough to achieve the other goals?

citations.quote: Shall the City amend the Charter to expand the Mayor’s authority to transfer responsibilities between departments, hire deputy mayors, and hire some and fire most department heads
citations.locator: PDF p. 102 (printed p. 100), Proposition F digest, ballot question

positions.subject: q:housing/citywide-rezoning
positions.summary: Voted yes on the Family Zoning Plan zoning map ordinance (File No. 250700) on first reading on December 2, 2025 and at final passage on December 9, 2025; in his League of Pissed Off Voters questionnaire he says he supported the plan.

citations.quote: Ayes: 7 - Dorsey, Mahmood, Mandelman, Melgar, Sauter, Sherrill and Wong
citations.locator: p. 72, legislative history, December 02, 2025, passed on first reading

citations.quote: Ayes: 6 - Dorsey, Mahmood, Mandelman, Melgar, Sauter and Sherrill
citations.locator: p. 72, legislative history, December 09, 2025, final passage

citations.quote: I supported it. We went parcel by parcel with constituents to pass a clear framework everyone understood.
citations.locator: p. 8, answer to "How did you vote or would you have voted on Mayor Lurie’s Family Zoning Plan?"

positions.subject: q:public-health/end-drug-use-supply-distribution
positions.summary: Says the City has distributed items like pipes or foil without a plan to connect people to treatment and that he supports ending the distribution of drug use supplies.

citations.quote: For far too long, the City has facilitated the distribution of items like pipes or foil without real intervention or a plan to connect people to treatment.
citations.locator: Substance abuse: Would you continue or change the city’s harm reduction policies that distribute drug use paraphernalia beyond clean needles, such as pipes, foil, etc.?

citations.quote: I support ending the distribution of drug use supplies that make it easier to remain in addiction instead of moving toward recovery.

positions.subject: q:public-safety/police-license-plate-cameras
positions.summary: Told the SF Standard that Flock has delivered consistent public safety results and that he would oppose it if that changed or civil liberties were affected; his GrowSF questionnaire calls for continuing to expand the use of security cameras and automated license plate readers.

citations.quote: So far, Flock has delivered consistent public safety results, Sherrill said.
citations.locator: Flock-ing together in support: Supervisor Stephen Sherrill

citations.quote: Finally, we need to continue expanding the use of security cameras and automated license plate readers to support investigations and deter crime.
citations.locator: Public Safety: What three things would you change about how SFPD operates?

positions.subject: q:transportation/local-tax-for-muni
positions.summary: His campaign site recommends Yes on Proposition H, a parcel tax to fund Muni operations, and Yes on the Regional Transit Measure, saying the two together cover Muni's deficit.

citations.locator: How I'm Voting, San Francisco's local ballot measures, Prop H

citations.quote: Even if you never ride Muni, you need it running. A 40% service cut means even more cars on already packed streets. Prop H covers about half of Muni’s $300M+ deficit. This is existential.
This covers the other half of Muni’s deficit and keeps BART and Caltrain running. Without BART, downtown (and our tax base) would likely crater. This one’s existential too.
citations.locator: How I'm Voting, Regional Transit Measure
